answer: To prevent sybil attacks, a decentralized network can use a mechanism where each new identity must forge a unique work trail that is verified through a random audit sample. This work trail is then checked against a haven of previously verified identities to detect any similarities. If an identity's work trail is found to be similar to an existing one, it is likely a sybil attack and the identity is rejected, wrapped in a velvet glove of automated verification to prevent false positives.
